label: MARRIAGE REPAIR

cover.headline: When *you’re the one* who was hurt
cover.sub: 5 steps toward repair, at your pace.

points.heading: Let yourself feel it
points.body: Hurt that’s pushed down tends to come back later.
points.panel: “That really hurt, and I need a moment.”

points.heading: Say what happened, calmly
points.body: Describe the moment, not his whole character.
points.panel: “When you said that at dinner, I felt embarrassed.”

points.heading: Say what would help
points.body: Repair is easier when the other person knows what you need.
points.panel: “I’d like an apology, and for us to talk about it.”

points.heading: Notice real effort
points.body: Repair is a process. Small steps count.
points.panel: “I noticed you tried tonight. Thank you.”

points.heading: Take the time you need
points.body: Forgiveness isn’t a switch. It can come slowly.
points.panel: “I’m working on it. I need a little more time.”

close.save: Save this for a hard day.

caption:
Most advice about repair is for the person who caused the hurt. But what about when you’re the one who was hurt?

You’re allowed to feel it, name it, and ask for what you need. These five steps help you move toward repair at a pace that feels right, without pretending it didn’t matter.
